mathematical_sources.title: Short-Cycle Decompositions and Full Zombie Damage in Cubic Graphs
mathematical_sources.note: End-to-end formalization of the main arbitrary-graph theorem, its exact bound and graph-to-strategy dependencies, with the recurrent-coverage, structural and expansion results. The separate sensing discussion around Remark 19 is supplementary library material, not part of the Comparator selection.

mathematical_sources.title: The Zombie Damage Number of a Graph
mathematical_sources.note: Randy Davila introduced the zombie damage number and the one-zombie game in Definition 1 and posed Conjecture 24. Lennart Rudolph formalized those rules and developed the complete conjecture proof with disclosed AI assistance. The numerical value is the maximal forceable damage score; its connection to the full-damage predicate and eventual semantics is proved. SOURCE_THEORY.md identifies the original source results formalized here. This project does not claim to formalize every theorem in the original paper.

mathematical_sources.title: Distance-Shell Tomography on Graphs: Integer Trades and Optimal Grid Sensing
mathematical_sources.note: Section 2 defines multiplicity-preserving labelled shell observations and bounded recovery. The supplementary library source encodes those semantics using lists modulo permutation and shortest-walk radii; no grid theorem is imported. No distance-shell result is selected by comparator.json.

mathematical_sources.title: Computing Metric Dimension of Two Types of Claw-free Cubic Graphs with Applications
mathematical_sources.note: Theorem 2 already gives metric dimension t for the ring of t>=3 diamonds and hence the paper's sensor lower bound. The central-pair and sensor-counting formalizations are supplementary known mathematics, not new sensor-bound priority claims and not selected by comparator.json.

mathematical_sources.title: The Graph Curvature Calculator and the curvatures of cubic graphs
mathematical_sources.note: The closed cubic classification is already known. Lemma 5.1 and Corollary 5.4 in arXiv:1712.03033v2 identify prisms and Möbius ladders via the curvature criterion. That closed classification and the earlier ring sensor bound are credited rather than claimed as new.

mathematical_sources.title: The damage number of a graph
mathematical_sources.note: Original ordinary-damage game, AJC 75(1), 1–16 (2019). Randy Davila introduced the zombie-restricted damage parameter. No ordinary-damage theorem is assumed by the proof.

mathematical_sources.title: Replacing Cops with Zombies
mathematical_sources.note: Related geodesic pursuit with a capture objective, FUN 2026, LIPIcs 366, 30:1–30:12. It does not resolve the damaged-vertex objective.

mathematical_sources.title: On the damage number of graphs
mathematical_sources.note: Ordinary one-cop damage, arXiv v1 of 15 August 2026; graph-family and complexity results. Cop moves are not constrained to be geodesic.

mathematical_sources.title: On the multi-robber damage number
mathematical_sources.note: Ordinary cop/multiple-robber damage; first posted in 2022, v4 revised 22 June 2026. Background only.

mathematical_sources.title: The damage number of the Cartesian product of graphs
mathematical_sources.note: Ordinary-damage background, AJC 88(3), 362–384 (2024); read together with the 2025 corrigendum.

mathematical_sources.title: Corrigendum to: The damage number of the Cartesian product of graphs
mathematical_sources.note: AJC 91(1), 217–218 (2025). Corrects domination definitions and affected ordinary-damage statements. No corrected theorem is a premise here.
